queries: why language models hallucinate training evaluation incentives
neurosymbolic structured knowledge eliminates hallucination evaluation

sources_considered.why: A leading 2025 analysis of what causes hallucination. It offers a competing account but does not test Marcus's necessity claim.

receipt.public_excerpt: language models hallucinate because the training and evaluation procedures reward guessing over acknowledging uncertainty

evidence_items.explanation: Gives a different cause of hallucination and a different fix: rewarding abstention. It is an argument, not a demonstration that hallucinations can be avoided without structured knowledge, so it does not settle the claim.

unresolved_gaps: No system of any architecture has been shown to avoid hallucinations reliably, so there is no test of whether structured knowledge is necessary.
No controlled study compares hallucination across architectures in a way that bears on necessity.
